data.title: Unauthenticated admin dashboard exposes client and business data
data.summary: Anyone can open the admin dashboard in a browser or with a simple request and see internal enquiry and client details. The site tries to send visitors to the login page using JavaScript, but the confidential page content is already sent first.
data.description:
Unauthenticated GET requests to `/dashboard` and `/dashboard.html` return HTTP 200 with the full "Admin Dashboard — Ausecurity" page (about 16 KB of HTML). The page includes an apparent signed-in admin view, enquiry lists, activity, and business figures such as revenue. Multiple client email addresses were present in the HTML. Those addresses are not repeated here.

The login API correctly rejects anonymous users (`GET /api/auth/me` returns 401 `Not authenticated`). Access control for the dashboard is only in client-side JavaScript in `/assets/js/main.js`, which redirects after the confidential HTML has already been delivered. Search engines, command-line tools, and anyone who disables JavaScript still receive the data.

Business impact: client contacts and internal pipeline information can be read by the public. This can enable phishing, competitor intelligence, and loss of client trust.
data.recommendation: Require a valid server-side session before returning any dashboard HTML or data. Return 401/302 from nginx or the application for `/dashboard` without a session cookie. Move dashboard data to authenticated APIs. Treat any data already exposed as potentially compromised and notify affected clients if the records are real.

data.title: DOM-based cross-site scripting on the consultation success page
data.summary: A crafted link can run an attacker’s script in a visitor’s browser on the “thank you” page. The contact form also puts the visitor’s name into that same page address.
data.description: `consultation-success.html` reads the `name` query parameter and assigns it to `innerHTML` with no encoding: `document.getElementById('user-name').innerHTML = userName;` The company name uses the safer `textContent`. `POST /api/contact` returns `redirect_url` including the attacker-controlled name (URL-encoded) and the front end navigates there. A direct visit such as `/consultation-success.html?name=` is enough; login is not required. The site has no Content-Security-Policy to limit script execution. Business impact: a client or staff member who opens a malicious link can have the page altered, be shown a fake message, or have their session used in the browser.
data.recommendation: Use `textContent` for the name, never `innerHTML`. Encode output. Add a strict Content-Security-Policy without `unsafe-inline`. Validate and length-limit contact fields on the server.

data.title: Open redirect after login via the redirect parameter
data.summary: After sign-in, the site sends the user to whatever address is in the `redirect` query parameter. A phishing page can be made to look like it started on Ausecurity’s login.
data.description:
`/assets/js/main.js` contains a comment “Safety check: only allow same-origin redirects” but then does `window.location.href = params.get('redirect')` with no allowlist, no leading-slash check, and no origin check. The same assignment runs if the user is already authenticated and visits `/login?redirect=...`. External URLs such as `https://evil.example/` are therefore accepted.

Business impact: attackers can use the real login page as a stepping stone to a lookalike site and harvest credentials or deliver malware.
data.recommendation: Allow only relative paths that start with a single `/` and do not start with `//`. Reject `http:`, `https:`, `javascript:`, and backslash variants. Perform the check in code, not only in a comment.

data.title: Self-signed TLS certificate
data.summary: The website’s HTTPS certificate is self-signed, so browsers will warn visitors and attackers on the network can more easily impersonate the site.
data.description:
The certificate subject and issuer are both `CN=ausecurity.best`. SAN lists only `ausecurity.best`. Validity is 2026-09-14 to 2027-09-14. SHA-256 fingerprint `B5:30:10:E0:32:E7:42:10:E4:B1:F0:68:A0:C5:B2:A2:0B:F6:44:C1:F3:32:92:87:4D:1C:64:07:14:8D:14:E2`. There is no public CA chain (for example Let’s Encrypt).

Business impact: clients may abandon the site, ignore future certificate warnings, or have their traffic intercepted.
data.recommendation: Issue a certificate from a public CA covering `ausecurity.best` (and www if used). Enable automatic renewal. Turn on HSTS after the trusted certificate is in place.

data.title: Missing HTTP security headers
data.summary: The website does not send standard browser-protection headers. That makes clickjacking, protocol downgrade, and script injection easier.
data.description:
A GET to `/` returned `Server: nginx/1.22.1` and no `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, or `Permissions-Policy`. HTTP `/` does redirect to HTTPS, but without HSTS a later visit can still be forced to HTTP. The unauthenticated admin dashboard can be placed in a third-party iframe.

Business impact: attackers can overlay or frame the admin view, weaken HTTPS, and have a wider window for the XSS issue above.
data.recommendation: Send HSTS (`max-age` at least 15552000, includeSubDomains) after a valid public certificate is installed. Add `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` or CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a strict Referrer-Policy.

data.title: HTTPS /api path redirects to HTTP
data.summary: Asking for the API folder over HTTPS sends the browser to an HTTP (unencrypted) address.
data.description:
`GET https://ausecurity.best/api` returns `301` with `Location: http://ausecurity.best/api/`. The site root correctly redirects HTTP to HTTPS, but this API slash-redirect drops TLS.

Business impact: a network attacker can intercept or change that follow-up request.
data.recommendation: Redirect to https://ausecurity.best/api/ and keep HTTPS. Prefer an nginx redirect that preserves the HTTPS scheme, the host, and the request URI. Disable HTTP except for the HTTPS redirect.

data.title: Missing SPF and DMARC records
data.summary: The domain publishes a contact address but has no mail authentication records, so others can more easily send email that looks like it came from Ausecurity.
data.description:
`dig` showed no MX, TXT, SPF, DMARC, or CAA records. The public site advertises `info@ausecurity.best`. With no SPF or DMARC, mailbox providers have little instruction to reject spoofed mail.

Business impact: clients may receive fake invoices, fake pentest reports, or credential-harvesting messages using the company name.
data.recommendation: If the mailbox is unused, do not advertise it. Publish `v=spf1 -all` and a DMARC policy (`p=reject` once monitoring is done). If mail will be used, add MX and a correct SPF include for the provider.

data.title: Web server version disclosed
data.summary: Responses include the exact nginx version, which helps attackers choose known bugs.
data.description: The `Server` header is `nginx/1.22.1` on HTML and JSON responses.
data.recommendation: Set `server_tokens off;` in nginx and hide version details in error pages.
